own_solution.law: The first law gives Q = ΔU + pΔV. With five excited molecular degrees of freedom, Cv = 5R/2; the ideal-gas law gives pΔV = nRΔT. Therefore Q = (7/2)nRΔT = 3491.88 J = 3.49188 kJ.
assumptions: The stated ideal-gas and molecular-excitation model applies throughout heating.
The gas amount remains fixed during heating, after any stated addition.

notes: All answers here are in kJ. For the relevant additions, Q = 1.74594(2 + q) kJ when q is expressed in mol, giving 4.714038, 5.761602 and 7.682136 kJ at the three listed amounts; the certified rounding is adequate. Both pressure cancellation expressions are correct, and all listed pressures are compatible with the stipulated ideal-gas model. The disconnected bottle and earlier run leave the current cylinder amount unchanged. The claimed numerical minimal pairs preserve 1.3 mol and change only the intended object or event attachment.
